r01_baseline.interpretation: The audit treats the latest accepted cumulative chain as baseline without rewriting its acceptance kinds. Current behavior is tested at the later target commit rather than inferred from historical reports.

findings.title: Public CodeWorker ASK projection and resume path is broken
findings.expected: A default interactive tool call that returns ASK is visible through /permissions/requests; exact approval resumes the parked call once. A second ASK in the same logical batch can be approved and resumed without replaying the first effect.
findings.actual: The repository-owned one-ASK test receives permission_suspended but the public pending queue is empty. The reviewer-owned two-ASK probe observes the same empty queue; retry then fails with 'restored tool call is missing its scheduled batch'. No side effect executes and no Python policy fallback occurs.
findings.risk: Normal interactive CodeWorker work that requires approval cannot proceed through the public API. This is P1 under the taskbook because it blocks the ordinary continuous batch path; fail-closed behavior limits unauthorized side effects but does not make the workflow usable.
findings.root_cause_status: not fully localized; the failure is at the cumulative TypeScript-owner/public-transport/checkpoint bridge, not in the low-level E02 decision tests

findings.title: Browser disclosure is not delivered into the current CodeWorker 02D provider envelope
findings.expected: A BrowserWorker disclosure claimed for the task is selected exactly once and appears in the real CodeWorker provider request/envelope with causal event ids.
findings.actual: Browser execution succeeds and reports one pending context item, but CodeWorker returns 409. selected_source_ids, provider_request_ids, provider_turn_ids and event_ids are empty; findings include provider_context_missing and provider_envelope_event_missing.
findings.risk: The user-visible cross-worker context handoff can silently stop the downstream CodeWorker path even though Browser-local tests and state creation pass. This is an ordinary cross-domain main-path blocker.
findings.root_cause_status: not fully localized; isolated reproduction rules out test-order contamination

findings.title: Root Python dependency/install manifest does not reproduce the tested browser runtime
findings.expected: A clean checkout can install project Python dependencies from an authoritative root manifest and run the applicable browser tests.
findings.actual: The root pyproject has no dependencies and editable installation fails because setuptools discovers multiple top-level packages. Three browser tests fail until vendor/browser-use[core] is explicitly installed into the fresh venv; all three pass afterward.
findings.risk: Environment reconstruction depends on undocumented prior state. This did not cause the two P1 semantic failures, but weakens reproducibility and release confidence.

subagent_planning_assessment.historical_pattern: Parent units M1-03A through M1-05D prescribe fixed role/prompt matrices. M1-06A uses the later generic optional subagent wording with gpt-5.6-sol xhigh only.
subagent_planning_assessment.causality_limit: No durable delegation transcript links either P1 directly to a particular subagent or to gpt-5.5. Model version and subagent-plan wording therefore cannot be named as the direct cause.
subagent_planning_assessment.evidence_based_conclusion: The fixed decomposition created a credible integration blind spot: local and owner-specific suites are strong, while two older public cross-domain tests regress after cumulative custody cutovers. Aggregate reviews previously caught several similar cross-boundary issues. The risk is fragmentation and missing cumulative regression selection, not proof that individual subagents produced low-quality code.
subagent_planning_assessment.model_version_assessment: No evidence supports a material gpt-5.5-specific failure. The observed defects are deterministic state/projection integration failures on the current code.
